SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
CONFIDENTIAL S.1, Special Branch
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY 9212 S. B. Div. 27 - 31）
Date May 20, 1939.

Subject (in full) Activities in National Salvation Propaganda (Persons,
organizations and schools)

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Herewith attached is a list of individuals,
organizations and schools etc., which came to the notice
of the Municipal Police during the period from January
to May, 1939, in connection with propaganda activities
of a national salvation nature. This list has been
compiled in accordance with the remarks of the Commissioner
of Police on the attached report relating to the issue
of posters with national salvation slogans by the China
Industrial and Commercial Artists' Society (Special Branch
Report dated May 9, 1939).

（批：The Attestation）

C. Crawford
D. I.

（批：D.C. (Sp. Br.) D.C. (Special Branch)
P.A. to D.C. (Sp. Br.)
21/5）

CONFIDENTIAL LIST OF INDIVIDUALS, BODIES, AND SCHOOLS ETC., WHICH CAME TO THE NOTICE OF THE MUNICIPAL POLICE DURING THE PERIOD FROM JANUARY TO MAY, 1939, IN CONNECTION WITH PROPAGANDA ACTIVITIES OF A NATIONAL SALVATION NATURE. 20.5.39 Name & address of organization | Responsible persons | Activities ---|---|--- Shanghai People's Spiritual General Mobilization Headquarters. (Secret organization). | (1) Tu Yueh Sung (杜月笙), in Hongkong.
(2) Yui Yao-chiu (余耀球), former secretary of local Tangpu.
(3) Doong Ying-pah(董行白), former committee member of local Tangpu (now defunct).
(4) Chang Hou(章豪), former member of Executive Committee of local Tangpu.
Director of the New Life Movement in Shanghai. | Made an attempt to promote the movement in Shanghai during April, 1939. Their activities were greatly curtailed by the local foreign authorities who took suppressive measures as soon as the movement was started.
On April 19, the local Chinese community hoisted National flags to mark the commencement of the movement in Shanghai. Minor incidents took place between shop-keepers and the French Police who prohibited the flag raising.
Yui Yao-chiu (No.2) was taken into custody by French Police at 12 Rue du Consulat on April 26, 1939, on suspicion of being concerned in disseminating propaganda. Released on 28.4.39.
Chang Hou (No.4) is reported to have been abducted together with several other Chinese at the Foo Lai Restaurant, 159 Kwangsi Road, on 9.5.39, by the Japanese Military Police. Shanghai Educational Circles' Spiritual General Mobilization Association. (Secret organization). | (1) Chen Che-chen (陳濟成), Committee member of S.M.C. and principal of Private Shanghai Middle School, 460 Chengtu Road.
(2) Woo Tse-ching (吳志青), principal of Shanghai Girls' University, 451 Taku Road. | This association distributed propaganda literature bearing on the movement to schools in the Settlement and French Concession during April, 1939.
(1) and (2) were warned by the Municipal Police on 1/5/39. They denied participation, and agreed to comply with the instructions of the Police.

Activities

Shanghai People General Mobilization Association.
(上海人民動員協會)
(Secret organization).

(1) Kang Zang Nai (康長祏), President.
(2) Li Tsoo Sung (李楚琛), Vice President, Ex-Sub-Inspector of the now defunct Public Safety Bureau.
(3) Boo Voong Ming (蒲風鳴), Vice President, Chairman of now defunct Chung Nyi Association in Nantao.
(4) Yang Dah Ziang (楊大祥), Chief of Organization Dept., Ex-Sub-Inspector of the now defunct Public Safety Bureau.
(5) Dien Kung (田耕), Chief of Propaganda Dept., Ex-Chief of Propaganda Dept. of Chung Nyi Association (now defunct).
(6) Zia Ki Sung (謝紀生), Chief of Social Affairs Dept.
(7) Zung Sao Ching (陰少慶), Chief of General Affairs.

A manifesto announcing the inauguration of this organization was issued on 29/3/39. The main object is to exhort the people (1) to follow the "Three Principles of the People", (2) to support the Government in its policy of fighting the Japanese to the bitter end, (3) to abide by the regulations governing the "People's Spiritual General Mobilization", (4) to join the guerilla activities and (5) to exterminate traitors.
Four corps (Students, labourers, traders and women) are reported to have been formed to function in their respective circles with the above object in view.

"Unwilling to Become Slave National Salvation Association"
(Maintains a secret address in Rue Gaston Kahn).

(1) Hwang Ching Wan (黃警頑), departmental chief of Commercial Press, Honan Road. (Committee member of the defunct "Vocational Circles National Salvation Assoc.")
(2) Sung Vung Kwei (沈文葵).
(3) Yao Sai Mei (姚瘦梅).
(4) Wong Tsung Hwa (王震華).

Fostering propaganda chiefly among local educational circles for the preservation of individual personality and a refusal to serve or cooperate with the Japanese but the continuance of support to the principle of fighting the Japanese to the bitter end with an undaunted spirit.
This Association was formerly located in the Settlement but was warned by Police to cease functioning immediately after its inauguration during November, 1937.

上海人民动员协会
(上海人民動員協會)
（秘密组织）。

(1) 康长祏 (音译)，主席。
(2) 李楚琛 (音译)，副主席，前已解散的公安局副督察。
(3) 蒲风鸣 (音译)，副主席，前南市忠义协会主席（该协会现已解散）。
(4) 杨大祥 (音译)，组织部主任，前已解散的公安局副督察。
(5) 田耕 (音译)，宣传部主任，前忠义协会（现已解散）宣传部主任。
(6) 谢纪生 (音译)，社会事务部主任。
(7) 阴少庆 (音译)，总务部主任。

该组织于1939年3月29日发布宣言宣布成立。其主要目标是劝勉民众：(1) 遵循“三民主义”，(2) 支持政府抗战到底的政策，(3) 遵守“国民精神总动员”的相关规定，(4) 参加游击活动，以及 (5) 铲除汉奸。
据报，已组建四个团（学生、劳工、商人和妇女），旨在各自圈层内以上述目标开展活动。

“不甘做奴隶救国会”
（在加斯顿·坎路 [Rue Gaston Kahn] 设有秘密地址）。

(1) 黄警顽，河南路商务印书馆部门主管。（前“职业界救国会”委员）
(2) 沈文葵 (音译)。
(3) 姚瘦梅 (音译)。
(4) 王震华 (音译)。

主要在当地教育界开展宣传，旨在保持个人人格，拒绝为日本人服务或与其合作，但以无畏的精神继续支持抗战到底的原则。
该协会原址位于租界内，但在1937年11月成立后立即受到警方警告，要求其停止活动。

Publishes a semi-monthly periodical entitled "Printer (印工)" (national salvation nature), copies of which have been surreptitiously distributed among the local workers in the printing trade.
Wong ordered the printing of the said periodical from the Chung Dong Printing Press during April, 1939.

Chung Dong Printing Press,
(中同), 6/357 Weihaiwei Road.
(1) Ho Yung Kung (何榮根), Manager.

Shanghai Municipality Two-Five (? Feb. 5.) Thrift & Gold Offering Groups.
(Address unknown).
Responsible persons unknown.
On April 4, 1939, small groups of boys and girls of the student type visited tea rooms, restaurants, etc. in the Central District of the Settlement and solicited contributions from customers for national salvation purposes. They claimed to be members of the "Two-Five Group" but their drive was confined to April 4, 1939, only.

Activities

-----
{1} Shen Ki (沈驥) alias.
{2} Shen Koo Jen (沈戈人).
Arrested by the French Police in front of Lane 514, Rue Amiral Bayle for chalking Anti-Japanese and communist slogans on the pavement on April 19, 1939. Known to the French Police as a "political disturber of the peace".

Local Women Circles.
(1) Miss Huang Ting Wei (黃定慧), Sub-Manageress of the Tung Yih Trust Co., 384 Peking Road.
(2) Miss Yang Mei Tseng (楊美珍), Vice-Chairman of Chung Hwa Women's Christian Temperance Association, 8C Love Lane.
(3) Miss Chiang Ping (姜平), Executive member of S'hai Women's Association, Room 512, Pootung Guild, Avenue Edward VII.
(4) Miss Tsu Vung Yang (朱文央), member of Executive Committee of Chung Hwa Women's Mutual Aid Society, Room 605 Pootung Guild, Avenue Road.
On March 5, local women representatives held a dinner on the premises of the Association Amicale Sino-Francaise, 577 Rue Lafayette, in observation of the International Women's Day (March 8). Resolutions bearing on the national salvation movement were discussed and passed, and handbills containing a song of a national salvation nature distributed among the attendance. The ladies mentioned formed the presidium at the meeting.

Students Service Society (學生服務社), Room 523, Pootung Guild, 1454 Av. Edward VII.
(1) Li Kwang Sz (李光世), ex-student of the Institute Technique Franco-Chinois, Rue Lafayette. At present unemployed; residing at 392 Rue Frelupt.
(2) Mao Ying (毛瑛), unemployed, residing at 34 Bei Tuh Li, Tatung Road.
Established at the beginning of May, 1939, ostensibly for the purpose of promoting the welfare of students and guiding them in conducting independent researches. Contemplated to form a "Ten Commandments Movement" on May 4, 1939, but the Society was warned by the Police to wind up on 3/5/39. The ten commandments required the students to refrain from frequenting cabarets and cinemas, drinking and gambling, reading harmful books and writing love letters, buying foreign goods and allowing themselves to be placed at the disposal of unscrupulous persons or to be enslaved by others.

3月5日，本地妇女代表在拉斐特路577号中法联谊协会会所举行晚宴，以纪念国际妇女节（3月8日）。会议讨论并通过了有关救国运动的决议，并向与会者分发了包含一首救国歌曲的传单。上述女士组成了会议主席团。

学生服务社 (學生服務社)，爱德华七世路1454号浦东同乡会523室。

成立于1939年5月初，表面上是为了促进学生福利并指导他们进行独立研究。曾计划于1939年5月4日发起“十诫运动”，但该社于1939年5月3日受到警方警告并要求解散。这“十诫”要求学生不得频繁出入歌舞厅和电影院，不得饮酒赌博，不得阅读有害书籍和写情书，不得购买外国货，不得任由无良之人摆布或受人奴役。

Middle School Department of Utopia University, 572 Rue Amiral Bayle.
- - - - -
Some of the students made an attempt on 1/5/39 to hold a meeting for the purpose of initiating the People's Spiritual General Mobilization Movement. The principal dismissed four students responsible for the arrangement.

In giving publicity to a
charity sale in the Sun Co. Building,
Nanking Road, between May 12 and
May 21, 1939, the Society issued
copies of a poster containing the
following slogans:-

"All should work for a deliverance
from the present national crisis!"
"Make united efforts to preserve
our existence!"

Wong Ye Chong was warned, and posters
were later surrendered to the Police.
The persons mentioned

charge of arrangements for the charity
sale.

propaganda.
